blurb:
Southern Fried Chicken, Pancake Paloozas, mimosas, and a live jazz duo every Saturday and Sunday from 11 to 3. C. Ellet's at The Battery does brunch the way it's supposed to be done.

This is a recurring thing, so it's not a one-night-only situation. But if you've been meaning to try it and haven't gotten around to it, October is a great time to make a reservation and actually go. The Battery is easy to get to from the Perimeter, the restaurant is a legitimate destination on its own, and a long jazz brunch on a fall Saturday is hard to argue with.

Make a reservation online before you head over.
scoring_notes: Strong demographic fit for the income level and adult-leaning audience. Docked significantly on uniqueness because this is a recurring weekly event, not a special occasion. Included because it's genuinely close to the coverage area and is a quality experience worth featuring as a secondary pick.

blurb:
150 arts and crafts booths, food vendors, live music, kids activities, and football on in the background while you walk around with a beer in hand. Smyrna's Crafts & Drafts is one of those fall festivals that earns its reputation year after year.

It runs Saturday from 10 to 6 and Sunday from noon to 5, so there's plenty of room to fit it into the weekend without committing your whole day. Smyrna Village Green is an easy drive from the Perimeter, and this is the kind of event that works for basically everyone: couples, families, people who just want to be outside and browse. Free admission means the only decision is whether to have one beer or two.

Worth putting on the calendar if you haven't been before.
scoring_notes: Mixed-audience friendly, geographically close, and fall timing is ideal. Annual recurring festival so uniqueness is moderate. Free admission is a plus for families but not a deciding factor at this income level. Broad appeal across the young families and young professional segments of this audience.

event_name: Amp It Up! Live Music Festival featuring Heart of Atlanta
blurb:
Free live music in Roswell on a Saturday morning, and the cause behind it makes it worth showing up. Amp It Up! is a music festival fundraiser supporting music therapy scholarships, and Heart of Atlanta headlines.

It's a relaxed, feel-good morning out with good music and a reason to be there beyond just the entertainment. The kind of thing you can walk into casually, stay as long as you want, and leave feeling like you actually did something with your weekend before noon.

No tickets, no cost. Just show up.
scoring_notes: Free outdoor music festival with a charitable angle fits the community-minded professional audience. Lower uniqueness score because free outdoor music is available most weekends in Atlanta. The cause and the specific band give it a slight edge. Morning time slot works well for the family-mixed audience.

event_name: Booze and Boos: Halloween Wine & Candy Pairing
blurb:
Five wines. Ten Halloween candies. Two treats paired per wine. At $10 a ticket, this might be the best value in Atlanta this month.

Deep Roots Wine Market on Marietta Square is hosting this pairing event the night before Halloween, and the concept is exactly as fun as it sounds. They're not just handing you a glass and a Snickers. It's a curated pairing experience that takes something silly and makes it genuinely interesting. Reese's with a Pinot? Someone has thought this through so you don't have to.

It's a great pre-Halloween night out, it's short enough that you can still make other plans after, and at $10 it's a STEAL. Grab a friend and go.
scoring_notes: Strong adult fit, fun and social format, extremely accessible price point. Halloween timing adds novelty. Unique concept (candy and wine pairing) separates it from standard wine events. Short 2-hour format is a practical selling point for busy professionals.

event_name: Rocky Horror Picture Show at The Strand
blurb:
The night before Halloween. A 1975 cult classic. Audience participation, costumes encouraged, and prop bags for purchase while supplies last. If you know, you know. If you don't, this is your year to find out.

The Strand Theatre in Marietta is hosting Rocky Horror as part of their Spooky Movies series, and this one is not a passive movie-watching experience. You show up, you dress up if you're feeling it, you get your prop bag, and you participate. Brad and Janet stumble into Dr. Frank-N-Furter's castle and the audience makes sure they know exactly how that's going to go.

It's a legitimately fun night out with the right people. Get your tickets early and wear something you won't regret.
scoring_notes: Strong adult skew, Halloween timing is perfect, and Rocky Horror has a natural appeal to the educated 30s-40s demographic who likely have nostalgia for it. The participatory format makes it more than just a movie night. Uniqueness score reflects that this is a recurring annual tradition at many venues, though it's still a genuinely special event.

event_name: Blacksmithing Skulls with Michael Dillon: This Too Shall Pass
blurb:
You show up. You put on an apron. You forge iron into a skull with your own hands. That's the afternoon.

Michael Dillon runs this hands-on workshop at Art Center West in Roswell, and the premise is exactly what it sounds like: a full-day sculptural blacksmithing experience where participants make Halloween-themed ironwork, no experience required. It's physical, it's creative, and it's genuinely not something most people have ever done. For a Saturday in late October, that's a hard combo to beat.

This is adult-only in all the best ways. A real skill, a real result you take home, and a story that's a lot more interesting than 'we went to a pumpkin patch.' If you've ever been curious about blacksmithing or just want to do something completely different this weekend, this is it.
scoring_notes: Highly unique hands-on experience, adult-skewing, fits well with the creative and experiential interests of a 38-median-age professional audience. Halloween timing adds relevance. Strong uniqueness score for a one-day workshop format.

blurb:
Darkened rooms. Embalming equipment from the 1800s. Mourning jewelry made from actual human hair. This is not your average Halloween event.

The William Root House opens its doors after hours for a special flashlight tour through rooms decorated for a Victorian era funeral. You'll walk through 19th century death and mourning customs up close, with all the eerie, fascinating artifacts that go along with it. It's genuinely weird in the best possible way, and it's the kind of thing you'll still be talking about at Thanksgiving.

Space is limited and they mean it. At $10 in advance, this is an easy yes. Grab your tickets before they're gone and leave the kids at home on this one.
scoring_notes: Niche, after-hours, adults-only Halloween event at a historic house. High uniqueness, strong fit for the educated adult audience that appreciates history and experiential events. Low ticket price is irrelevant as a barrier but makes it an easy impulse buy.

blurb:
You tour Bulloch Hall, the antebellum home where Teddy Roosevelt's mother grew up, and then you walk over to Mimosa Hall and spend the evening with the 26th president himself. Not a documentary. Not a lecture. A living history performance where Roosevelt tells his own stories in first person, right there in the room with you.

This is the kind of event that sounds like a good idea and then turns out to be a genuinely great night. The setting alone is worth showing up for. Mimosa Hall at dusk in October is not something you stumble into on a random Saturday. And the combination of a historic house tour followed by a theatrical performance from one of American history's most outsized personalities makes this feel like a real outing, not just a thing to do.

Tickets are limited and the venue is intimate, so if this sounds like your kind of evening, don't sit on it.
scoring_notes: High-income, highly educated audience skewing adult makes this a strong fit. Unique living history format, beautiful historic venue, one-night-only event. Adult-skewing with no family conflict. Price is unlikely to be a barrier at this income level.

event_name: Spooky Movies at The Strand: Beetlejuice (1988)
blurb:
Beetlejuice is one of those movies where you can recite half the dialogue and still want to see it on a big screen. Tim Burton's 1988 original, rated PG and absolutely wild from start to finish, is screening at The Strand on Saturday, October 24th, with a live pre-show concert on the Mighty Allen Theatre Organ before the film kicks off.

This one works for almost any combination of people in your house. Teens who've only seen the sequel, adults who saw it in theaters the first time, and anyone in between. The Strand is a beautiful room for it, and the organ performance opening the show gives the whole thing an atmosphere you won't get anywhere else.

Note: North and East Park Streets will be closed for a Glover Park Concert happening the same evening, so Waddell Parking Deck is your best bet. Plan for it and you'll be fine.
scoring_notes: PG rating opens this up to families with teens, which fits the East Cobb mixed demographic well. The Beetlejuice 2 release in recent years refreshes interest in the original. Live organ pre-show is the differentiator. Slightly lower uniqueness score because there are multiple Spooky Movies events this month at the same venue.

event_name: Silent Films at The Strand: The Phantom of the Opera (1925)
blurb:
Here's something you genuinely cannot replicate at home. The Strand, in partnership with the American Theatre Organ Society, is screening the 1925 silent film classic The Phantom of the Opera on Sunday, October 25th at 3pm, with live accompaniment performed on The Strand's Mighty Allen Theatre Organ the entire time.

This is the way these films were originally meant to be experienced. A live musician reading the scene and scoring it in real time, on a full theatre organ, while Lon Chaney's phantom stalks the catacombs of the Paris Opera. It's cinematic history presented the way it was built to be shown, and there are very few places in the country where you can walk in off the street on a Sunday afternoon and see that.

This is a low-key Sunday but a high-quality experience. Good for a first date, good for a spouse who loves something a little unexpected, good for any East Cobb resident who wants a great story to tell Monday morning.
scoring_notes: Highest uniqueness score of the Strand film series events. Live organ accompaniment for a 1925 silent film is genuinely rare. Appeals to the educated, culturally-engaged portion of the East Cobb audience. Sunday afternoon 3pm slot is relaxed and accessible. Slightly lower demographic fit because silent films have a narrower but devoted audience.

event_name: Spooky Movies at The Strand: A Nightmare on Elm Street (1984)
blurb:
There are horror movies, and then there are the ones that genuinely changed how the genre works. A Nightmare on Elm Street is firmly in the second category. Wes Craven's 1984 original, the one that introduced Freddy Krueger and launched a young Johnny Depp, is screening at The Strand on Thursday, October 22nd, with a live pre-show concert on the Mighty Allen Theatre Organ starting 30 minutes before the film.

Watching a classic horror film in an actual theater, on a proper screen, with a live organ performance opening the night, is a totally different experience than whatever streaming version you've half-watched on the couch. The Strand was built for this kind of thing. It's a great October night out.

Rated R. Anyone under 17 needs a parent or guardian. Grab tickets early, the Spooky Movies series at The Strand tends to sell.
scoring_notes: October 22 is technically valid (on or after Friday the 16th, Thursday the 22nd qualifies). 1984 horror classic hits the sweet spot for the 42 median age audience who grew up with this film. Live organ pre-show elevates it above a standard screening. R rating means it's an adult night out, which suits the audience well.

event_name: Spooky Movies at The Strand: Halloween (1978)
blurb:
The night before Halloween, you're watching Halloween. That's just how it should work. John Carpenter's 1978 original is screening at The Strand on Thursday, October 29th in a restored and remastered digital print, supervised by cinematographer Dean Cundey himself. This isn't a fuzzy DVD rip on a big screen. It's the real thing, done right.

And yes, there's a live pre-show concert on the Mighty Allen Theatre Organ before the film. The Library of Congress selected this film for the National Film Registry in 2006 for its cultural significance, which is a very formal way of saying it earned its place. Jamie Lee Curtis's star-making performance, Carpenter's score, the tension that builds without relying on cheap jump scares. It holds up.

Rated R, under-17 needs a parent or guardian. October 29th in a historic theater watching one of the defining horror films ever made. Hard to beat that.
scoring_notes: October 29 timing is near-perfect for Halloween week. Restored/remastered print is a genuine differentiator from just watching it at home. 1978 film aligns well with the 42 median age audience who grew up watching it. Adult skew via R rating fits the audience. Strong competitor with the Nightmare on Elm Street entry but the Halloween timing gives it an edge.

blurb:
Beck is one of those artists who has never really stopped being interesting. From Loser in '94 to Sea Change to Colors, he keeps shifting and somehow keeps landing. He's coming to Coca-Cola Roxy on Friday, October 30th, which also happens to be Halloween eve, and that's not a bad way to spend it.

The Roxy is the right-sized room for this. Big enough for real production, small enough that it still feels like a concert and not a stadium event. It's at The Battery, so dinner before the show is an easy add, and parking is manageable if you plan for it (note: road closures go into effect before large events, so factor in a few extra minutes).

If Beck has been on your radar for 30 years and you've never caught him live, this is the night to fix that.
scoring_notes: Beck's era aligns almost perfectly with East Cobb's median age of 42. The Battery location is familiar and accessible to this audience. Halloween timing adds a social hook. Adult skew is strong, which fits well. Ticket price at a venue like the Roxy is well within range for $118K households.

blurb:
Halloween Hikes at Chattahoochee Nature Center has been running for 41 years, and the reason it keeps selling out is simple: there's nothing else like it in this area. You grab your event map, head out on a self-guided trick-or-treat hike through the Nature Center after dark, work through The Haunted Quest, and take in the evening activities. It's spooky in a way that actually works for all ages, not just little kids, not just adults.

This is running all three nights: Friday and Saturday, October 23–24 from 6–10pm, and Sunday the 25th from 5–9pm. If you've got teens at home who think they're too old for Halloween stuff, this will change their mind fast. And if the kids are out of the house entirely, it's still a genuinely fun night out with the nature setting doing a lot of the work.

Tickets include everything: the hike, The Haunted Quest, and all evening activities. Go ahead and grab them now. This one fills up.
scoring_notes: 41-year tradition gives it credibility and local familiarity without being generic. All-ages format hits the mixed family/empty nester crowd well, especially families with teens. Located just outside East Cobb in Roswell, very accessible. Annual event but the 41st anniversary and seasonal uniqueness make it worth featuring.

event_name: GPG Presents: A Celebration of Pink Floyd
blurb:
If you grew up with The Dark Side of the Moon on the turntable, this one is going to hit. Dark Side of Time, the Georgia Players Guild's tribute to Pink Floyd, takes the stage at The Strand on Friday, October 23rd, and these guys don't just play the songs. They recreate the full experience, from the Syd Barrett era all the way through The Division Bell, with the sound, the staging, and the atmosphere that made Pink Floyd impossible to imitate.

The Strand is a great room for this. Intimate enough that you're not watching a concert through a phone screen 200 feet away, but big enough that the production lands the way it should. Showtime is 8pm, doors open at 7pm.

If you want to go all in, the VIP package includes early access seating, a pre-show mini-concert, meet and greet with the band, two drink tickets, and a signed poster. That's a real night out, not just a concert. Grab tickets before they're gone.
scoring_notes: Pink Floyd's peak era is squarely in the 40-55 demographic wheelhouse. The Strand is a beloved local venue, and a high-quality tribute at that level is genuinely special. VIP option is attractive to the $118K median income crowd. Strong adult skew, which fits the empty nester portion of the audience well.

blurb:
This is the one fall weekend event that actually earns the label. The City of Kennesaw's Pigs & Peaches BBQ Festival runs all day Saturday, October 17, from 10am to 10pm, and the lineup this year is legitimately stacked. Tigirlily Gold, the ACM Award-winning duo, kicks things off at 6pm, and platinum-selling singer-songwriter Chayce Beckham headlines at 8pm. That's a full evening of live country music, and it's included with general admission.

But the music is almost secondary to the vibe. BBQ vendors, a full day of food and activity, and the energy of a downtown festival done right. This is the kind of Saturday where you show up early, eat too much, and end the night on your feet at a live concert. Bring the family, grab a spot, and let the evening come to you.

Admission is FREE. You don't need a reason beyond that, but Chayce Beckham and a plate of brisket is a pretty good one anyway.
scoring_notes: Annual festival but this year's headliners (Chayce Beckham, Tigirlily Gold) elevate it significantly. Free admission is a bonus but not the selling point for this audience. Country music + BBQ + downtown festival is a near-perfect fit for East Cobb's family/empty nester mix. First weekend event after newsletter sends, so timing is ideal.

blurb:
If you've never done Trap Karaoke, the premise is simple and the execution is chaotic in the best possible way. You get up, you sing trap and hip-hop classics, and the crowd goes with you. It's part concert, part comedy show, part group therapy for anyone who's had a long week and needs to let something loose.

The Coca-Cola Roxy at the Battery is a legitimately great venue for this. Good sound, good energy, and enough room that the crowd itself becomes part of the show. This runs from 6 PM to 11:30 PM so you've got the whole evening if you want it, or you can roll in later and catch the back half.

Grab a few people, make a reservation if you can, and go. This is the kind of Friday night that's a lot more fun than whatever else you were planning.
scoring_notes: Median age of 38 and young professional skew is a strong match for Trap Karaoke's demographic sweet spot. The Battery is close to the Perimeter area. Adult-only event works for this newsletter's audience. Recurring format at this venue slightly dings the uniqueness score, but it's not a weekly series and remains a high-energy adult night out that fits the audience well.

blurb:
Southern Post in Roswell is doing fall the right way on Saturday afternoon. Pony rides, a petting zoo, live music, and game day vibes from 2 to 5pm, which is honestly an ideal Saturday afternoon block if you've got younger kids in the mix or grandkids visiting for the weekend.

It's a quick drive from East Cobb and Southern Post is a genuinely nice development, so even if you've been before for dinner, this is a different kind of afternoon. Wrap it up by 5 and you've still got your evening free. Easy win for a Saturday in October.
scoring_notes: Lower uniqueness score because pony rides and petting zoos are fairly standard fall festival fare. The East Cobb audience skews toward teens and college-age kids, so this lands better for grandparents with visiting grandkids than for the core audience. Still a real, specific event within the window and worth including as the eighth option given limited qualifying candidates.

blurb:
Smyrna is doing Halloween right on Friday night, and it's completely free. The Spooky Festival takes over Market Village with trick-or-treating, a DJ, spooky decorations throughout downtown, and a Pet Parade starting at 6:30pm (if you've got a dog who needs a costume moment, this is their Super Bowl).

Once the parade wraps, they're screening "It's the Great Pumpkin, Charlie Brown" followed by "KPop Demon Hunters" on the big screen at Village Green. No registration required, all ages welcome, and you don't have to spend anything to make it a full night out. It's the kind of Friday where you just show up and let the evening happen.
scoring_notes: Solid fit for East Cobb families with younger teens who still enjoy Halloween-themed community events. Free admission and a no-registration-required format lowers the barrier to attendance. The pet parade angle adds a fun, shareable element. Loses some uniqueness points because Halloween community events are common in October, but the outdoor movie double feature gives it a specific hook.

blurb:
If you've got someone in your house who knows every word to Arcángel's catalog, Thursday night at the Roxy is going to be a very big deal. The Puerto Rican reggaeton and Latin trap artist is one of the most decorated voices in the genre, and he's bringing the show to the Battery on October 15th.

The Roxy is a great room for this kind of show, big enough to feel like an event, tight enough that the energy actually builds. Tickets are available now. If this is your thing, or your kid's thing, this is one worth getting off the bench for.
scoring_notes: Arcángel is a legitimate Latin music star with a real fanbase. Demographic fit is more niche for East Cobb's median 42-year-old audience, but the audience skews family with teens and college-age kids, and this is exactly what that demographic listens to. Included because uniqueness is high and the audience's kids likely drive demand here.

blurb:
If you need a plan for Friday night, Kennesaw's got you. The 2026 Pigs & Peaches BBQ Festival takes over Downtown Kennesaw from 6 to 10pm, and it's exactly what it sounds like: big BBQ energy, live music, and a crowd that's there to have a good time.

It's a short drive from East Cobb and the kind of event where you don't need a reservation, a plan, or a reason. Just show up hungry. Whether you're grabbing the family or going out with neighbors, this is an easy Friday night that actually delivers. Four hours of festival, and it wraps up before it gets late. Hard to argue with that.
scoring_notes: BBQ festivals are familiar territory for this audience and fit the family-plus-established-adults mix well. Close proximity to East Cobb is a real plus. Loses some uniqueness points because BBQ festivals are a recurring regional staple, but an annual city-hosted festival still qualifies as a real event worth flagging. Friday evening timing works for most households.

event_name: Choral Festival Performance: KSU University Choirs
blurb:
KSU's Bailey Performance Center is one of the genuinely great concert halls in the metro area, and on Tuesday the 20th it's hosting something worth the weeknight trip. A collection of KSU's university choirs will perform music by Detroit-based composer Stacey V. Gibbs, best known for his arrangements of spirituals that bring new energy to familiar works without losing what makes them powerful.

If you've ever been to Bailey and seen a choir performance in that room, you know it hits differently than a recording. For East Cobb households with a KSU connection, or anyone who appreciates choral music at a high level, this is a quiet Tuesday that punches well above its weight. Check the KSU website for timing and ticket details.
scoring_notes: KSU is embedded in the East Cobb community and Bailey Performance Center draws a loyal audience from this area. The 65% college-educated demographic skews toward appreciation for choral and classical performances. Weeknight timing is the main trade-off, but East Cobb residents are close enough that a Tuesday evening is manageable. The Stacey V. Gibbs focus gives it a specific artistic identity beyond a generic choir concert.

blurb:
This one started as neighbors deciding to show each other what they'd been making in their garages and backyards. Forty-something artists later, the Cherokee Heights Arts Festival has become one of the more genuine community events in Cobb County, and it happens right in Marietta on Saturday.

Freyer Drive NE turns into an outdoor gallery for the day, with over 40 local and neighborhood artists set up alongside live music and food. No ticket needed, no admission. Just show up, walk around, and see what people in your community are actually creating. It runs 9am to 4pm, so there's plenty of time to pop in for a couple hours and still have your afternoon.

If you've got a teen who needs a nudge toward something that isn't a screen, this is a low-pressure, genuinely interesting way to spend a Saturday morning.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for educated, community-oriented East Cobb households. Free admission removes any friction. Saturday daytime works for both families with teens and empty nesters. The neighborhood-roots story gives it character that a generic arts fair wouldn't have. Proximity in Marietta is a genuine plus.

venue: Earl and Rachel Smith Strand Theatre, Marietta
blurb:
The Strand Theatre is one of those venues that makes you feel like you actually live somewhere worth living. And on Saturday night it's hosting something genuinely special: Strand Ole Opry's Bluegrass Roots show, two hours of authentic bluegrass featuring some of the best pickers in the southeast.

We're talking tight harmonies, real instrumentation, and classics like "Foggy Mountain Breakdown" and "Blue Moon of Kentucky" performed by people who actually love this music. The vocalists are local performers who volunteer their time to keep this tradition alive, which makes the whole thing feel like something you discovered, not something sold to you.

It runs 8 to 10pm, right in Marietta, which means you could grab dinner first and make a full Saturday out of it. This is exactly the kind of night you'll be glad you didn't skip.
scoring_notes: Strong fit for the East Cobb audience's age profile and appreciation for live arts. The Strand is a beloved local venue. Bluegrass skews toward established, educated audiences rather than young families. Saturday evening timing is perfect. Not a recurring weekly event, though the Opry series does run periodically, making this a solid but not rare pick.

event_name: Legacy and Groove – A Tribute to Earth, Wind & Fire
blurb:
If you remember exactly where you were the first time you heard "September" or "Shining Star," this one is going to hit different.

The Ray Howard Band is back at the Roswell Cultural Arts Center with their full Earth, Wind & Fire tribute show, and they already SOLD OUT the last time they did this. That's not marketing copy, that's just what happened. The band brings the full sound, the horns, the harmonies, the groove, all of it. This is the kind of live music experience that East Cobb is close enough to make completely effortless on a Saturday night.

Doors open at 6pm. This is a real night out for two people who deserve one. Don't sleep on it.
scoring_notes: Earth, Wind & Fire's catalog lands squarely with the 40+ demographic that makes up the core East Cobb audience. The sold-out prior show signals strong demand. Short drive from East Cobb. Adult skew is a perfect fit for established couples and empty nesters. Saturday evening timing is ideal.

event_name: Apollo to Artemis: To the Moon and Back Again
venue: Tim D. Lee Senior Center, Marietta
blurb:
A NASA Solar System Ambassador walking you through America's past, present, and future plans for the Moon, Mars, and beyond. That's the pitch for Tuesday afternoon at the Tim D. Lee Senior Center, and honestly it's a pretty good one.

This is a one-hour presentation covering the full arc from Apollo to the Artemis program, which is actively working to put astronauts back on the Moon. If you're the type of person who watched the documentary, or has kids who came home from school talking about Mars missions and couldn't answer their questions as well as you wanted to, this is worth the hour. A NASA Ambassador presenting locally is not something that happens every week.

Free to attend, Tuesday at 2 PM in Marietta. A smart afternoon out if you can swing it.
scoring_notes: NASA Ambassador presentations are legitimately uncommon at the local level. East Cobb's highly educated audience skews toward science and technology interest. Weekday afternoon timing limits appeal somewhat (rules out working adults, better for retirees and empty nesters with flexibility). Senior Center venue may undersell the event's broad interest potential, but the content itself is broadly appealing. Free and nearby.

blurb:
The inaugural Cumberland Art Festival lands this weekend at Galleria on the Park, presented by Genuine Parts Company, and it's a first-year event worth showing up for.

This one is brand new, which means nobody's jaded about it yet and nobody knows exactly what to expect, which is actually a reason to go. Art festivals that stick around usually stick around because the first one was worth repeating. Creativity, community, and culture in one of the more underrated green spaces in the Cumberland district. Easy to get to from East Cobb, free to walk in, and the kind of afternoon that pairs well with dinner somewhere nearby after.

Get there early, see what they built, and you'll have an opinion on it before everyone else does.
scoring_notes: Inaugural events carry natural uniqueness weight. East Cobb's educated, higher-income audience skews toward arts and culture. Cumberland/Galleria is a familiar destination for this demographic. Summary is thin so some uncertainty on programming depth, but the inaugural angle and proximity make it a solid inclusion. Free admission removes friction.

event_name: HarvestFest and Scarecrows in The Square
blurb:
Marietta Square does fall better than almost anywhere in the metro, and HarvestFest is the proof.

Saturday brings the full lineup to Glover Park: arts and crafts show, Touch-A-Truck, a costume contest, a Pie Eating Contest from Pie Bar, and the Scarecrows In The Square competition spread throughout the park. There's also a College Football watch party setup called the Big Chicken Cornerback's Coop, which is exactly as fun as it sounds. Bring your chairs and your drinks and stake out a spot.

If you've got younger kids still at home, this covers everything they want. If the kids are grown and you just want to walk the Square on a crisp October Saturday with something actually happening around you, that works too. Free to attend, easy to make a half-day of it.
scoring_notes: HarvestFest hits East Cobb's mixed family profile cleanly, activities for younger kids, atmosphere for adults, and a football watch party that bridges both groups. Marietta Square is a natural East Cobb destination. Annual event but with enough programming variety to justify inclusion. Free admission is a practical plus for families.

blurb:
Two days of smoked meat, live music, and 100-plus vendors taking over downtown Kennesaw. Thats what the Pigs & Peaches BBQ Festival brings every year, and it's right up the road.

Friday kicks things off at the United Bankshares Amphitheater at Depot Park and along Main Street. You've got established and rising musical acts, festival food from across the Southeast, drinks, shopping, and enough BBQ to make questionable decisions you won't regret. It's a full festival setup, not a food truck pop-up. If your crew hasn't been before, this is the year.

Parking is available throughout downtown Kennesaw. Free to walk in, easy to spend a few hours. Just bring a real appetite.
scoring_notes: Annual event with genuine scale (100+ vendors, multi-stage music) that plays well for established families and empty nesters alike. East Cobb is close enough to Kennesaw that it's a realistic Friday evening outing. Free admission lowers friction for groups. BBQ festival format skews broad demographic appeal. Not a one-of-a-kind event, but the scale and proximity make it worth including.

event_name: Legacy and Groove: A Tribute to Earth, Wind & Fire
blurb:
This show sold out last time. The Ray Howard Band is back, and if you missed the first run, here's your second chance.

Legacy and Groove is a full-band tribute to Earth, Wind & Fire, which means September, Shining Star, Got to Get You Into My Life, and the full catalog delivered with live horns, real vocals, and the kind of energy that makes it physically impossible to stay in your seat. The lobby opens at 4:30 for a silent auction benefiting the Roswell Organization for Community Development, so you get the chance to give back before the show even starts.

This is a real concert at a great venue, not background music at a festival. Roswell Cultural Arts Center keeps it intimate enough that every seat feels close. If you need a Saturday night plan that your group will still be talking about on Sunday, this is it.
scoring_notes: Earth, Wind & Fire's catalog lands squarely with the 38-55 demographic that makes up the East Cobb core. Sold-out prior run signals strong demand and adds urgency. The charity component adds meaning beyond entertainment. Roswell is a natural East Cobb adjacent destination. Strong adult couple or group night-out fit.

event_name: Strand Ole Opry: We Will Always Love Dolly
blurb:
Dolly Parton gave the world a lot. The songs, the Imagination Library, the laugh, the rhinestones. Honoring all of it in one night sounds about right.

The Strand Theatre is hosting a heartfelt tribute to Dolly's life and music on Saturday night, with community singers and a live house band working through the songs that made her legendary. Expect harmonies, sequins, and probably a few tears, because Jolene hits different when it's live. This is warm, local, and built around a woman whose music crossed every generational line.

Marietta Square on a Saturday night in October is already a great reason to get out. Add a Dolly tribute inside one of the most beautiful small theaters in the metro area and you've got a real night out. Grab your tickets and bring someone who knows every word.
scoring_notes: Dolly Parton spans generations but lands especially hard with the 38-55 crowd. The Strand is a premium local venue that East Cobb residents regularly drive to. Saturday night timing is ideal. The tribute nature of the show makes it emotionally resonant, not just a generic live music night. Strong empty nester and established family adult-night-out fit.

event_name: Mother of a Monster: Mary Shelley's Frankenstein
blurb:
If you've ever been curious about where Frankenstein actually came from, not the green face paint and neck bolts version, but the real story behind one of the most haunting novels ever written, this is the night to show up.

Dr. Molly Livingston from Kennesaw State University is bringing her course on British Gothic literature to life at the William Root House on Thursday evening. She'll walk through the personal tragedies, the scientific obsessions, and the romantic idealism that pushed a teenage Mary Shelley to write a book that still defines horror and science fiction nearly 200 years later. It's a one-hour lecture, intimate and focused, and space is LIMITED.

This is the kind of thing you don't stumble into again. A historian walking you through one of literature's great origin stories, inside a 19th-century historic home, in October. The timing could not be more perfect. Don't sit on this one.
scoring_notes: East Cobb skews highly educated (65% bachelor's or higher) and 42 median age, which maps well to a literary/historical lecture. The KSU connection is local credibility. Limited space makes it genuinely can't-miss. October timing amplifies the Gothic theme. Strong adult skew is a fit for empty nesters and couples looking for a smart night out.

blurb:
There are art festivals and then there's this one: 40-plus neighbors and local artists setting up on a single block of a 1924 National Historic Register neighborhood, once a year, for one day only.

The Cherokee Heights Arts Festival is the kind of boutique show that doesn't feel like a festival at all. It feels like being invited somewhere. Original paintings, woodwork, pottery, photography, jewelry, textiles, baked goods, and more from local artists who don't sell like this anywhere else. Two music stages anchor both ends of the block with live local performances all morning and afternoon. Beer on tap. A kids' art activity from the Marietta/Cobb Museum of Art. Real holiday gifting potential if you keep your eyes open.

No admission, free parking, one mile north of the Square. It runs 9 to 4 and it only happens once a year. Saturday is genuinely the only shot.
scoring_notes: Annual one-day boutique arts festival in a historic neighborhood is a near-perfect fit for East Cobb's educated, higher-income, arts-appreciating demographic. The combination of local authenticity, free admission, live music, beer, and holiday shopping angles covers empty nesters and established families equally. One-day-only urgency is real. Proximity to Marietta Square makes it an easy yes.
